## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Kūṭavāṇijajātaka* (Ja 98) is a birth story in the Pali *Jātaka* collection, placed within the *Bhāṇavagga* (*Bhasanavaggo*) [Anandajoti 2010]. The framing narrative is set at Jetavana, where the Buddha delivers the teaching in reference to a dishonest merchant [Fausböll 1877]. In the story of the present, two partners from Sāvatthi travel together to sell goods and return home with their earnings [Fausböll 1877].

In the story of the past, the Buddha recounts how a deceitful merchant named Superwise attempted to defraud his partner, the wise merchant (the Bodhisatta), over the division of their profits [Anandajoti 2010; Fausböll 1877]. Superwise concealed his own father inside a hollow tree to impersonate a tree deity (*rukkhadevatā*) and render a fraudulent judgment in his favor [Anandajoti 2010]. Suspecting deception, the Bodhisatta set fire to the hollow tree, causing the scorched father to flee from the blaze; the two merchants subsequently divided the shares equally [Anandajoti 2010; Fausböll 1877]. The canonical verse begins with the line *Sādhu kho paṇḍito nāma* ("Wise rightly, Wisest wrongly") [Fausböll 1877].
